mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement 'X gives N to Y' appears, subtract N from X and add N to Y, updating each person's count accordingly.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement explicitly says that one person gives a certain number of items to another.
mathgap.example: Incorrectly adding N to X and subtracting N from Y (reversing the transfer direction).

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a distinct variable for each person and translate every relevant statement (counts, differences, transfers, relational equations) into linear equations, then solve the system simultaneously.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains multiple constraints linking the quantities of different people.
mathgap.example: Treating each equation in isolation and not linking variables across constraints.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: Interpret any comparative phrasing that mentions a difference—such as 'X has more than Y', 'X has N more than Y', or 'the difference between X and Y'—as a signed difference X − Y, preserving the order given.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a difference between two quantities.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has more than Y' as |X - Y| (absolute difference) instead of X - Y.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Apply all transfer statements (including gifts, conditional transfers, splits, and redistributions) to update counts before setting up and solving relational or difference equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a problem contains both transfer statements and relational statements.
mathgap.example: Solving relational equations before applying the effects of transfers.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: Treat statements that give an explicit count (e.g., 'X has N items') as the initial amount for X before any transfers are applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a problem provides explicit starting quantities.
mathgap.example: Assuming the given count is the final amount after transfers, ignoring subsequent transfers.

mathgap.title: Answer formatting
mathgap.principle: Output the final answer using the exact required format: 'The final answer is \boxed{<integer>}' with no extra characters.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the end of solving, before returning the result.
mathgap.example: Providing the answer without the \boxed{} wrapper or with extra text.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form 'If X has more than N items, X will transfer their items to Y', first evaluate the condition using the current counts, then apply the transfer only if the condition holds.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer is conditional on a person's count.
mathgap.example: Applying the transfer regardless of whether the condition is satisfied.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative increase handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'The number of X increases by a/b times', interpret it as multiplying X's current count by (1 + a/b) (i.e., X becomes X * (1 + a/b)).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a problem describes a multiplicative increase.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'increase by a/b times' as adding a/b instead of multiplying.

mathgap.title: Equal distribution handling
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form 'X and Y redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount', set both X and Y to the average of their combined total (i.e., (X + Y) / 2).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a problem mentions equal redistribution between two parties.
mathgap.example: Assuming each keeps their original amount instead of equalizing.

mathgap.title: Nested signed difference handling
mathgap.principle: When a relational statement equates a phrase like 'the number of X that Y has more than Z' to a phrase like 'the difference between the number of A and B', interpret both sides as signed differences preserving the order given (Y - Z = A - B).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever an equality involves nested signed difference phrasing on both sides.
mathgap.example: Treating the statement as |Y - Z| = |A - B| or swapping the order on the right side (interpreting as A - B = Y - Z).

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the given count is the final state, not recognizing that transfers modify the counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret direct count statements as initial amounts before any transfers, and apply transfer updates afterwards.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: Misreading the phrasing 'X gives N to Y' and swapping the roles of X and Y.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a statement says 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: Confusion between magnitude of difference and directional difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order given in the statement and interpret it as X - Y.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by X times' as multiplying by X
mathgap.why_it_happens: Misreading the phrase 'increase by' as a direct multiplication factor.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'increase by X times' as X times the original amount added to the original (i.e., new = original * (1 + X)).

mathgap.description: Incorrect handling of equal distribution statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: Assuming each retains their original amount or miscalculating the average.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Compute the total of both parties, divide by 2, and assign that value to each.
